statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F = z\vec i + 6 x\vec k through the parameterized surface S oriented upward and given, for 0\le s\le 2, \ \ 2\le t\le 5, by x=s^2, \quad y=2s+t^2, \quad z=4 t.

static.solution:
\partial \vec r / \partial s \times \partial \vec r / \partial t is given by \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial s}\times\frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial t}= \left|\begin{array}{ccc} \quad\vec i\quad\amp \quad\vec j\quad\amp \quad\vec k\quad\\ 2s \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 2t \amp 4 \end{array} \right| = 8\vec i- 8 s\vec j+4st\vec k. Since the z-component, 4st, of the vector \partial \vec r / \partial s \times \partial \vec r / \partial t is positive for 0 \lt s \leq 2, 2 \leq t \leq 5, we see that \partial \vec r/\partial s \times \partial \vec r / \partial t points upward, in the direction of the orientation of S we were given.
Thus, we use d\vec A = \left(\frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial s} \times \frac{\partial \vec r}{\partial t}\right)\,ds\,dt, and so we have \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{2}\int_{2}^{5} (4 t\vec i + 6 s^2\vec k)\cdot (8\vec i- 8 s\vec j+4st\vec k)\,dt\,ds =\int_0^{2}\int_{2}^{5} (32 t + 24 s^3 t)\,dt\,ds = \int_0^{2}(16 t^2 + 12 s^3 t^2)\bigg|_{t=2}^{t=5}\,ds =\int_0^{2}(336 + 252 s^3)\,ds=(336s + 63 s^4)\bigg|_0^{2} =1680.
